title: Sort Array By Parity
prompt: Given an integer array `nums`, move all the even integers to the beginning of the array, followed by all the odd integers. Return any array that satisfies this condition — the relative order within the evens or within the odds does not need to be preserved.

examples.explanation: [4,2,3,1], [2,4,1,3], and other orderings would also be accepted.

hints: Building a new array of evens then odds works but takes O(n) extra space — can you rearrange in place instead?
This is the classic 'partition' step from quicksort, partitioning by parity instead of by a pivot value.
Use two pointers from each end: advance the left one while it's already even, advance the right one while it's already odd, and swap the two elements found stuck out of place.

solution.approach: Use two pointers, lo starting at the front and hi at the back. Advance lo past any elements that are already even, and move hi past any elements that are already odd. When both pointers stop, nums[lo] must be odd and nums[hi] must be even (each is 'stuck' in the wrong half), so swap them and continue. This is the same in-place partition technique used in quicksort's Lomuto/Hoare schemes, applied to a parity predicate instead of a pivot comparison, giving O(n) time and O(1) space.
